body: Badge reader at the Sector 4 entrance is blinking red. It won't let me or 8980 clock in. Had to get the night security guard to manually open the turnstile.
Funny how the IT system always breaks when we try to clock IN, but never when we try to clock OUT! 🤣 I'll let HR know to adjust our timesheets later.

Starting morning shift. Four days of production this week. Friday is August 1st, so the plant is closed. I expect maximum focus so we can all enjoy the long weekend without leaving a mess behind. Bühler SORTEX is booting up.

Did anyone watch the Euro final in Basel yesterday? England vs. Spain. What a match! I can't believe it went all the way to a penalty shootout. England defending the title was incredible. The atmosphere in the city was crazy.

BOOT SEQUENCE INITIATED > Unit: Bühler SORTEX Optical Sorter > Firmware: v4.1.2 > Checking Peripherals... > Camera 1 (Top): OK > Camera 2 (Side-A): OK > Camera 3 (Side-B): OK > Illumination Array: OK > Belt Drive: OK [SYSTEM_KERNEL] SYSTEM READY. WAITING FOR BATCH.
1691, yes! I was at the public viewing near the stadium. The tension during the penalties was unbelievable. Half the crowd couldn't even look. Anyway, I'm checking the hopper, looking good.
Hold everything! Before we start the feed, I almost forgot. Today marks exactly 35 years since 7290 started working at AlpenHarvest! 35 years!

Happy work-anniversary to 7290! She brought three massive, freshly baked butter Zopf breads for the morning team. She just told me that when she started in 1990, they didn't even have optical sorters. They had to pick out the bad peas by hand while listening to cassette tapes.
Charge_ID 88 arriving from Gate A. TransAlp. Euro-Pool pallets. Forklift is feeding it into the hopper now.
Belt speed set to 1.5 m/s. Everything sounds normal. Enjoy the Zopf, guys, I'm watching the screen.
Line 3 is running, but the yield monitor is flashing yellow. Total yield is at 84%. That's way below our 97% baseline.

4786, I'm watching the belt from the catwalk. The good peas are mostly passing, but on the far left side of the belt (Zone 1), the ejector is going crazy. It's just rapid-firing and blowing perfectly good, green peas into the reject bin.
I see it. The left side is a warzone. I am recalibrating the color thresholds for Zone 1 via the UI. Dropping the green sensitivity slightly to see if it relaxes.
Charge_ID 89 arriving from Gate B. SpeedyLogistics.
Recalibration didn't work. The SORTEX is still rejecting about 40% of the material on the left side of the belt. The right side and middle are perfectly fine.
We are wasting prime material here. I just checked the reject bin. It's full of A-grade Royal Garden peas. If we keep this up, we'll lose tons of product before the holiday.
The reject bin is already 80% full. Usually, this takes four hours. I am swapping it out for an empty one.
Hey guys, maybe the Earth's magnetic field shifted over the weekend and is interfering with the left sensor array? I read an article about solar flares affecting optical equipment.
5402, go count the empty pallets in Sector 2. Do not come back until you are done.

I am looking at the machine logs remotely. The software is definitely triggering the ejector on Zone 1. It's not a ghost-fire. The camera is seeing *something* it doesn't like, or the software threshold is corrupted.
Bringing more empty bins to Line 3. You guys are chewing through them.

Don't worry about the machine, kids. Machines have bad Mondays too. Have another slice of Zopf. I am putting a chair next to the reject bin and I will start hand-sorting the good peas out of the bad ones until Maintenance figures it out. I haven't done this since 1996! This is nostalgic.

Yield is still terrible. Left side rejecting non-stop. I have adjusted every threshold in the UI. Color, size, shape, density. Nothing changes the behavior of Zone 1. I am logging a priority ticket for Maintenance.

Ticket received. If the software settings aren't fixing it, it has to be a mechanical issue with the pneumatic manifold on the left side. The valves might be stuck open or the pressure regulator for Zone 1 is blown. I will come down during the shift handover.
I'm sampling the good output. The quality is flawless. But the volume is terrible.
We have 6 full bins of mixed rejects now. We need to help 7290 start hand-sorting them or they will go to animal feed.
I set up a table near the packaging line. 8980 and I are manually sorting the bins to rescue the good peas. This is extremely slow. 7290 is beating us both combined.

Handing over to afternoon shift. Line 3 is limping. Yield is 83%. We are bleeding good peas. 7290 is still sitting there hand-sorting, humming Swiss folk songs. Maintenance is taking over. Good luck, Katya.
Afternoon shift on. What a mess.

I have to put this in the log again: Messy handover from the morning shift. Urs, please tell your guys to throw away their empty coffee cups. Also, I just found a 10mm wrench sitting right on the catwalk railing. Someone could have easily kicked it into the hopper and destroyed the grinder. Keep it clean!
Locking out Line 3. I am dismantling the left-side ejector manifold.
Charge_ID 90 in from TransAlp. I have to hold it in the freezer staging area because Line 3 is down for maintenance.
While the line is down, 2130, 8779 and I are helping with the hand-sorting. My eyes are crossing from staring at green dots.
Someone burned popcorn in the breakroom microwave. The whole floor smells like smoke.
Manifold rebuilt. I cleaned all 32 nozzles on the left side, replaced three O-rings that looked a bit worn, and checked the pressure lines. It took three hours but it's spotless. Restarting Line 3.
Line 3 running. ...And the left side is still rapid-firing. The fix did absolutely nothing. Yield is 83%.

Are you kidding me? The pneumatics are perfect. If it's not mechanical, and it's not the UI thresholds, then it's a deep software bug in the camera processing. Tech Support needs to look at this tomorrow.
We're just running it as is. We have to clear the backlog. The reject bins are overflowing. We'll have to manually sort the rejects tomorrow too.
Delivering 10 more empty bins. Sector 4 looks like a warehouse for plastic boxes right now.
My back hurts from bending over the sorting table.
There are squashed peas all over the floor around the hand-sorting table. I'm mopping it up.
End of shift. What a frustrating day. At least it's only 3 more days until the holiday.
Morning shift. What a night. Those thunderstorms were absolutely biblical. The lightning was shaking my entire apartment block. Arrived at the plant and half the parking lot is flooded.
BOOT SEQUENCE INITIATED > Unit: Bühler SORTEX Optical Sorter > Checking Peripherals... [SYSTEM_KERNEL] ERROR: I/O TIMEOUT ON SENSOR BUS. [SYSTEM_KERNEL] KERNEL PANIC. ABORTING BOOT.
Line 3 will not boot. The screen just goes black after 10 seconds.
BOOT SEQUENCE INITIATED > Unit: Bühler SORTEX Optical Sorter > Checking Peripherals... > Camera 1 (Top): FAIL - NO RESPONSE [SYSTEM_KERNEL] KERNEL PANIC. ABORTING BOOT.
I am looking at the main power logs remotely. We had a massive power surge at 03:15 AM due to a lightning strike nearby. The UPS systems caught most of it, but the PLCs are acting completely dazed.
Just got a radio call from Sector 5. Line 4 is completely dead. Not even a standby light.
I'm over at Line 4 right now. The main transformer for this entire line is fried. I can actually smell ozone and melted copper. Line 4 is not booting today. Probably not tomorrow either.
Good morning! Wow, what a storm! That thunder reminded me of the great hail storm of '99. That year, the roof leaked right over the old packaging station. I see Line 3 is being stubborn. Let me try.

7290 just walked up to the dead SORTEX console. She didn't type anything. She just patted the side of the metal housing twice, exactly on the corner bracket, and pressed the green physical start button.

BOOT SEQUENCE INITIATED > Unit: Bühler SORTEX Optical Sorter > Checking Peripherals... > Camera 1 (Top): OK > Camera 2 (Side-A): OK > Camera 3 (Side-B): OK > Illumination Array: OK > Belt Drive: OK [SYSTEM_KERNEL] SYSTEM READY. WAITING FOR BATCH.
I... I have no engineering explanation for what just happened. But Line 3 is online. I'll take it.
Charge_ID 91, TransAlp, Gate B. Euro-Pool. We are routing all Line 4 traffic to Line 3 now because Line 4 is a paperweight.
Yield is still 83%. The left side is still rejecting everything. I'm going back to the hand-sorting table with Marie.
Eating leftover Zopf from yesterday while hand-sorting peas. Not a bad Tuesday.

Tech Support here. Looking at the Bühler SORTEX Zone 1 issue from yesterday. Maintenance says pneumatics are fine. Shift Lead says thresholds are fine. This means the algorithm itself is corrupted for Zone 1. The spatial weighting array in the neural net must have desynchronized.
I agree with 4356. We are going to SSH into the PLC, dump the current model weights, and flash the factory default firmware. Then we'll re-upload the custom AlpenHarvest model. Halting the line.
I am testing the hand-sorted bins. The operators are doing a good job rescuing the product. Passed QC.
Since the line is stopped, I brought croissants!
Put the croissants on the table and step away from them, 5402. We have Zopf today anyway.
Firmware flash at 80%. Taking longer than expected over the local network.
Firmware flashed. V4.1.2 reinstalled. Spatial matrices cleared and rebuilt. Rebooting the system.
Taking my lunch break. Just three more days.
System online. Running a test batch.
It is still broken. Zone 1 is still ejecting perfectly good peas. It is firing exactly as much as yesterday.
That is computationally impossible. We completely wiped the memory. The model is pristine. There is no software reason for it to target the left side of the belt.

I don't care if it's computationally impossible. My reject bins are full of gold-standard peas. Management is asking questions about the drop in overall plant efficiency, especially with Line 4 being dead.
Don't panic, kids! I brought my ergonomic sorting stool from 1998 out of storage. I will sit at the end of the line and catch the good peas. Everyone grab a bucket. It's like a harvest festival!
We are running diagnostics on the gigabit switch. Maybe packet loss on the camera feed for Zone 1 is causing the PLC to assume the missing data is a defect? We are replacing the ethernet cables.
7290 is an absolute machine. She is sorting twice as fast as me and 4031 combined. She isn't even looking at her hands.

Handing over to afternoon shift. Techs are under the machine swapping cables. Yield is terrible. 7290 is currently telling 5402 a story about how the CEO used to drive a tractor. Katya, the floor is yours.
Afternoon shift. Katya here. It's chaotic. And Urs actually cleaned up his coffee cups this time. Thank you.
Charge_ID 92 arriving from Gate B.
New cables installed by tech. Didn't fix it. The left ejector is still shooting like a machine gun.
The forklift beeper in Sector 2 is stuck on. It's been beeping continuously for 40 minutes. It's driving us insane over here at Line 3.
Sorry about the beeper. Forklift is isolated and turned off. Mechanic coming tomorrow.
My fingers are green. Literally stained green from the peas.

We have exhausted all software troubleshooting protocols. The firmware is clean, the network is clean, the data streams are completely synchronized. The algorithm is behaving exactly as it should based on the pixel data it receives.
So if the software is fine, and the mechanical ejectors are fine, why is it shooting good peas?
We don't know. We are escalating this to Bühler corporate support tomorrow morning.
Sweeping up under the hand-sort table.
End of shift. We are hand-sorting the rejects to save the good peas. Everyone's back hurts except 7290, who stayed two hours overtime because she said she was "in the zone".

Morning shift. Yield is 82%. Bühler corporate is supposed to remote into our system today. We have to keep the line running to meet the pre-holiday quota, even if it means hand-sorting the rejects. And we have extra load because Line 4 is still offline waiting for a transformer from Germany.
My hands are cramping before the shift even really starts.
Charge_ID 94, TransAlp, Gate A. Double volume because of Line 4.
The sheer volume of peas coming down this belt is terrifying.
I am so tired of hand-sorting. My fingers are green.

Chin up, everyone! This is good for hand-eye coordination. Back before we had automatic defect tracking, we had to sort 5 tons a shift by hand. Build some character! Also, I brought Rivella for everyone. It's in the breakroom fridge.
Bühler Level 3 support is on the VPN. They are running a remote deep-scan of the optical matrices.
I had to reject one of the hand-sorted bins. Someone let a small piece of corn stalk slip through. You guys need to pay attention, even if you are tired.
Two more days until the bonfire! I bought all the fireworks yesterday. The big Vulkan fountains.

Bühler support just got back to us. They say the raw telemetry from Camera 3 (which covers the left side) shows a persistent high-contrast artifact in the bottom left quadrant. The software is interpreting this artifact as a massive, continuous defect.
What does "high-contrast artifact" mean in normal language?

It means the camera thinks it is seeing something bad. But the camera diagnostics show the lens is perfectly functional. Bühler thinks the camera sensor itself might be dying. They are overnighting a replacement camera unit. It will arrive tomorrow.
So we suffer for another 24 hours. Great.
We've had to put three extra people on the reject bins just to salvage the good peas the machine is throwing away. It's slowing down the whole floor.
I keep telling 4031 to use the "scoop and flick" wrist motion. It's all in the wrist. If you use your whole arm, you'll be tired by noon!
I don't have anywhere to put these full bins. The staging area is completely full.
Swept the floor around Line 3. There are peas everywhere. The reject bins keep overflowing before the guys can hand-sort them.
Shift over. New camera arrives tomorrow. Keep hand-sorting. Good luck, afternoon team.
Afternoon shift. Yield is 81%. This is brutal.
Taking over the sorting table.
I'm trying the scoop and flick. It actually works. Thanks 7290!
My back is killing me. Hand-sorting 2 tons of peas because a camera is broken.
Charge_ID 95 arriving. Gate B.
Charge_ID 95 tested. The peas that *do* make it through the left side are fine. The machine is just hyper-aggressive.
I dropped a bucket of sorted peas. I wanted to cry, but I just swept them into the feed bin.
We are running out of empty crates for the sorted rejects. Logistics, we need more empty Euro-Pool crates at Line 3!
Bringing a stack of 50 empty crates now. Hang in there.
Just a few more hours. Tomorrow is the last day before the holiday.
End of shift. One more day until the long weekend. Please let that camera arrive early.
Morning shift. Last day before the August 1st holiday. Everyone wants to go home early. If that camera doesn't arrive by noon, I am going to lose my mind. Line is running. Hand-sorting continues.
I can already smell the bratwurst in my mind. Just 8 more hours of this.
Scoop and flick. Scoop and flick. I will hear this in my dreams.
Charge_ID 98, SpeedyLogistics, Gate B. No packages from Bühler on the morning courier truck.
Unbelievable.
I brought my special holiday playlist. We are listening to Swiss accordion music until that camera arrives. It makes the hand-sorting go faster! I promise!
The accordion music is actually helping. Or maybe I'm just going crazy.
Hey Urs, since we're waiting for the part, I was looking at the machine.
5402, do not touch anything.
I didn't touch it! I just used the flashlight on my iPhone to look inside the illumination chamber under Camera 3.
And? Did you find the dying pixel matrix?
No, but there is a dark brown, crusty spot right on the inside of the glass. It looks like a burned fingerprint.
...What?
Wait. Halting the line. I'm coming down.

I don't believe this. 5402 is right. Someone must have touched the inside of the protective glass with a greasy mechanic's glove during the last deep clean. The intense heat from the LED array slowly baked that grease into a solid, dark brown smudge right in the bottom left corner of Camera 3's field of view.

The camera was perfectly fine. The algorithm was perfectly fine. The software was seeing the baked grease spot, and because the belt is moving in the background, the optical illusion made the system think it was seeing a continuous, never-ending stream of brown, defective peas passing by on the left side.
I spent four hours rebuilding a pneumatic manifold because of a dirty fingerprint.
I wiped the entire memory of the PLC because of a dirty fingerprint.
I unlatched the glass. I wiped the smudge off with industrial solvent. It took exactly three seconds. Restarting the line.
I haven't laughed this hard since the forklift drove into the mayonnaise vat in 2012! Oh, my sides hurt. I hope whoever left that fingerprint was wearing gloves, or we can dust it for prints!
Yield is 99.1%. The left ejectors are completely quiet unless a real bad pea comes through.
5402. Good job. You can have a croissant today.
Good that we have changed to the digital shift log in the last digitalization initiative. Everything is documented down to the second.
Yeah, very reliable. Just a month ago we lost two weeks of entries and IT is still trying to recover them from the backup server. 🙄
Reject bins are looking completely normal. No good peas being wasted. We can stand down the hand-sorting team. You can pack up your ergonomic stool, 7290.
I am stretching my back. I feel like a new person.
Canteen is doing a pre-holiday BBQ outside! They have real St. Galler Bratwurst. Morale is instantly restored.
The bratwurst was amazing. And no more sorting. Best day ever.
Production is flying. We are catching up on the quota quickly since we aren't throwing away 15% of our product anymore. And Line 3 is handling the overflow from Line 4 like a champ.
Moving out the pallets twice as fast now. Logistics is happy.
Handing over to the final shift of the week. The machine is flawless. The smudge is gone. Enjoy the evening. Happy August 1st everyone.
Afternoon shift. Taking over. Belt at 1.5 m/s. Everyone is in a great mood. Music is playing on the floor.
I am just standing here watching the machine work perfectly. It's beautiful.
Last truck of the week just unloaded. We are shutting the loading dock doors.
Washing the green stains off my hands with industrial soap.
Last batch of Royal Garden is in the hopper.
Hopper is empty. Line 3 is clear. Yield finished at 98.8%.
Secured the machine for the long weekend. I locked the camera housings. No more greasy fingers are getting in there.
Shutting down the power to the main drive. Have a fantastic National Day, everyone! Grill some sausages for me.
Final deep clean of the floor finished. Swept up the last of the hand-sorted peas. Locking up Sector 4.
INITIATING STANDBY MODE. > Peripherals offline. > Core temperature nominal. [SYSTEM_KERNEL] SLEEP.
STATUS: SECURE. MODE: HOLIDAY LOCKDOWN. NOTE: SWISS NATIONAL DAY (BUNDESFEIER).
AUTOMATED PING. STATUS: GREEN.
AUTOMATED PING. STATUS: GREEN.
AUTOMATED PING. STATUS: GREEN.
AUTOMATED PING. STATUS: GREEN.
WEEKLY LOG EXPORT INITIATED...

Starting morning shift. Shift rotation is in effect! My team is on the early shift this week, and 4786 (Urs) and his team are taking the late shift. Hope everyone had a good long weekend for the August 1st public holiday. The fireworks over the lake were great, but reality is back.

BOOT SEQUENCE INITIATED > Unit: Bühler SORTEX Optical Sorter > Firmware: v4.1.3 > Checking Peripherals... > Camera 1 (Top): OK > Camera 2 (Side-A): OK > Camera 3 (Side-B): OK > Illumination Array: OK (Intensity: 97%) > Belt Drive: OK (Tension: 448N - Warning) > Packaging Link: OK (Tape Module: Low Warning) [SYSTEM_KERNEL] SYSTEM READY. WAITING FOR BATCH.

First batch of Royal Garden in from Logistics. TransAlp truck, Euro-Pool pallets. The Bühler ejector sounds asthmatic. Pfft-pfft instead of a sharp crack. We need maintenance here before we start the main run.
Checked the ejector manifold on the SORTEX. Found a frozen chunk of pea-dust blocking nozzle 4 and 7. Cleared with compressed air. Also, who keeps taking my 10mm wrench?
Charge_ID 2 arriving from Gate B. TransAlp. RFID Tag E84ECC40E9E42D96 scanned successfully. Feeding into the hopper.
Warning light on the end-of-line packaging machine. It says the 50mm clear tape roll is at 5%. I'll check the cabinet.
The cabinet is completely empty. No tape. I'm calling Logistics.

Received call from 1632. I checked the main warehouse. We are out of the standard AlpenHarvest branded tape. Procurement messed up the order before the holiday. I am looking for alternatives in Sector 2.
Machine performing weirdly. The belt speed is fluctuating. Setting says 1.5 m/s, but visually it looks like it's surging to 2.0 then dropping. Peas are clumping.
Packaging machine just ran out of tape completely. Alarm is sounding. The cardboard boxes are coming out open.
Stopping the SORTEX line. Hopper is full because we can't pack the accepted peas. 8461, where is the tape?!
I found two boxes of generic clear tape in the basement storage. It's unbranded and looks a bit old, but it's 50mm. Bringing it to Line 3 now.
Loaded the generic tape into the packaging machine. Restarting line.
The generic tape is garbage. It's too thin. The automatic tensioner on the box sealer is snapping the tape every 5th box. I have to manually re-thread it through the rollers every time it snaps.

Checking "Feature 12 overflow". It's the density sensor array. I rebooted the peripheral controller. Seems the sensor gets confused when two peas are stuck together with ice. Adjusted the mechanical shaker frequency from 40Hz to 45Hz to break up the ice clumps before they hit the SORTEX belt.

Sample from Charge_ID 2 checked. Good crunch, color is within AlpenHarvest spec. But found a small piece of blue plastic. Looks like a shard from a Euro-Pool pallet. Telling logistics to inspect the pallets from Gate B.
Tape snapped again. Re-threading. We have 40 open boxes piling up on the conveyor.
Canteen menu today: Zueri Gschnetzlets but the meat looks like old shoe leather. Taking my break now.
Taking over tape duty from 2130. This is a nightmare. The tape adhesive is leaving a sticky residue on the cutting blade. It's jamming.
Machine halted for 10 minutes. I have to clean the cutting blade with industrial solvent. The cheap adhesive is gumming up the springs.
SpeedyLogistics truck at Gate A. Charge_ID 1. Euro-Pool. Plastic shard issue communicated to the driver. He just shrugged.
Tape snapped. Re-threading.
Someone dropped a whole crate of grade B peas under the walkway of Line 3. It's a slip hazard. Cleaned it up.
Handing over to afternoon shift. Line is mostly okay but the tape situation is critical. 8194 is practically living inside the packaging machine. Good luck Urs.
Afternoon shift starting. Taking over.

I have to put this on the record immediately: Messy handover from the morning shift! 7662, your team left the packaging area looking like a sticky warzone. There are torn pieces of tape everywhere, a solvent rag left on top of the PLC monitor, and empty paper cups on the control panel. I spent my first 15 minutes cleaning up your mess. Clean up after yourselves next time!
Tape snapped. Re-threading.
What did you guys do to the UI? Half the text on the screen is in French now. "Vitesse du tapis"?
Sorry 8980, that was me. The firmware update yesterday reset the locale settings for some reason. I'll switch it back to German at the next pause.
Blade jammed with glue again.
Cleaning the tape blade with solvent. Production paused. We are losing so much throughput to this packaging issue.
Charge_ID 1 is running. Quality is dropping. The camera is rejecting perfectly good peas. The rejection bin is filling up way too fast.
Looking at the SORTEX camera feeds. Camera 2 is seeing shadows as dark spots because the overhead hall lights are flickering. The ballast in the ceiling fixture above Line 3 is failing.

I can't reach the ceiling fixture while the machine is running. For now, I've taped a piece of cardboard to the side of the machine to block the flickering light from hitting the belt. It looks stupid but the yield went back up to 96%. (And yes, I used the terrible thin tape to hold the cardboard, it barely sticks).
Tape snapped.
Machine halted. Alarm: CAMERA 2 DESYNC.

Camera 2 desync issue. I opened the casing. The vibration dampener on the camera mount is cracked. The camera was shaking so much the software couldn't focus, so it threw a desync error. Replaced dampener with a spare from Line 2. Rebooted.
Charge_ID 3 arrived. TransAlp. Euro-Pool.
Running smooth again. Yield is at 94%. Tape hasn't snapped in 40 minutes, a new record.
Spoke too soon. Tape snapped.
Shutting down for the night. Line 3 is clear. Cleaners are coming in.
2130, I told you! The system never fails when you clock OUT, only when you clock IN. It's programmed to steal our overtime! 🤣
Morning shift. Yield 94%? Unacceptable. I'm recalibrating the color thresholds. And who taped a piece of cardboard to the Bühler machine?! Taking it off.
Loaded a new roll of the generic tape. We only have 8 rolls left from what 8461 found in the basement.
Thresholds adjusted. R_val < 40, G_val > 180. Let's see if we can get this back to 98%.
7662, you took off the cardboard, now the yield is dropping again because of the flickering light. I am putting the cardboard back until 1577 replaces the bulb.

Just read the internal newsletter. Did you guys see the news from the UN conference in Geneva yesterday? They are drafting a massive agreement to reduce single-use packaging in global food supply chains. Management is thrilled. They said our switch to 100% reusable Euro-Pool pallets for incoming logistics puts AlpenHarvest way ahead of the curve. It's nice to see we're doing the right thing for the environment without having to change our processes again!
Tape snapped. Threading it back.
Charge_ID 4 arriving from TransAlp. Gate A. Plastic Pallets this time. RFID BFD98D5F9A1D1DAD.
Tape snapped. The roll is completely warped.
I adjusted the tension springs on the packaging machine to the lowest possible setting. Maybe it will stop snapping the thin tape.

Machine is acting weird again. The accepted peas have ice crystals on them. The freezer tunnel before the sorter is running too cold, causing frosting. The SORTEX thinks the white frost is a defect and is rejecting them.
Adjusted freezer tunnel temp. Bypassing the optical sorter's "white pixel" rule for the next 20 minutes to let the frosted batch pass, otherwise we lose 2 tons of good peas.
4356, bypassing the rules is how we end up with animal feed in Migros bags. I'm watching the belt manually. If I see a bad pea, I'm pulling it by hand.

Lowering the tension spring didn't help. The tape didn't snap, but because there's no tension, the tape is just loosely drooping over the boxes and not sealing them. Half the boxes are popping open on the palletizer.
Tightened the spring back up. We'll just have to deal with it snapping.
7662 dropped a lot of peas on the floor while "pulling them by hand". Swept it up.
Tape snapped. That's the 6th time today.
Handing over. Urs, try not to complain about the tape, we're doing our best.
Afternoon shift starting. Line 3 is running at 1.5 m/s. Humidity is steady at 45.0%.
Hey Urs, I was trying to take a slow-motion video of the ejectors firing for my university report.
5402, get your phone away from the belt right now.
Dave dropped his iPhone into the hopper. It went down the belt and the SORTEX immediately shot it into the reject bin.
Well, the machine correctly identified the iPhone 15 as a "Defect". Dave is currently digging through 50kg of rejected peas to find it. Production is unaffected.
Why is the UI blinking "Maintenance Required: Lubricate Bearings"? We did that last week.
The PLC counter for operating hours is bugged. It thinks it's been running for 8000 hours since last week. I just hit clear. If you hear grinding, let me know.
Blade is jammed with glue again. I'm not calling maintenance, I'll just scrape it with a box cutter.
Weird readings from Charge_ID 5. The peas are unusually small. The system isn't rejecting them, but they don't look like standard grade.
Hearing a slight grinding noise from the main drive drum. Not too loud, but noticeable.
...okay I'll come down and actually grease the bearings.
Tape snapped. We only have 3 rolls of this garbage left.
End of shift. Bearings greased. Yield stable at 97.5%.
Bearings sound fine today. But the UI language keeps randomly switching to French every 10 minutes. "Vitesse du tapis" again. As long as the Bühler sorts, I don't care what language it speaks.
Morning. We are on the second to last roll of tape.
Charge_ID 6, TransAlp, Gate B. Euro-Pool. RFID 728ABC49F9BB6BB1.
Line 3 is ghost-ejecting. Nothing on the belt, but the air valves are firing randomly. Pfft... pfft... pfft. It's wasting compressed air.

Ghost-ejecting is caused by dust on the background reference plate. The camera sees a dust spec, compares it to the threshold, thinks it's a brown spot on a pea, and fires. Fix: Removed the glass screen, wiped down the reference plate with isopropyl alcohol.
Tape snapped. Re-threaded.
I brought Gipfeli for the team to survive the tape disaster! They are in the breakroom.
Procurement update: The supplier for the branded tape is still out of stock. But they sent us an emergency pallet of substitute tape. It just arrived at Gate B. Sending it to Line 3.
The new tape is here. Wait. This is brown paper packing tape. The kind with the dry glue on the back that you have to wet with a sponge to make it sticky.
Are you kidding me? Our automatic box sealer doesn't have a water-wetting module. It only takes plastic pressure-sensitive tape. We can't use this paper tape in the machine.

Checking the logs. Because the PLC keeps switching locales, the CSV export is using commas instead of dots for decimals. The data lake is rejecting our uploads. We need IT to lock the region settings.
The last roll of the clear generic tape just ran out. We are completely out of usable machine tape.
Stopping the SORTEX line. Hopper full.

I am not letting Line 3 sit idle all day. 1632, 2130, grab damp sponges. We are going to wipe the brown paper tape by hand and seal the boxes manually at the end of the conveyor. Restarting the Bühler.
Machine weirdness: The "Total Sorted" counter on the UI is going backwards. It went from 12,040 kg to 11,900 kg.
The counter variable is an unsigned integer and someone set the offset to a negative value in the calibration menu. *cough* 5402 *cough*. Fixed it.
My hands are completely covered in wet, sticky starch glue. Manual taping is too slow. The boxes are backing up on the conveyor.
The sponge is getting too dirty, the glue isn't activating properly. The boxes are popping open. I'm switching to a wet rag.
We have to run the SORTEX in micro-batches. Run for 20 minutes, pause for 10 minutes to let 1632 and 2130 catch up with the manual taping. This is 19th-century factory work.
Shift over. The SORTEX is running. We are hand-gluing boxes. Have fun, Urs.
Afternoon shift. Everything looks green, except the guys covered in brown paper tape.
Taking over manual taping. This paper tape smells weird when it gets wet.

Tape rolls feel warm enough. Loading them into the machine.

Line 3 smells like burning rubber.

The packaging tape just jammed. The blade on the tape machine is completely covered in crusty brown glue from yesterday's wet paper tape experiment.

Checked the timing delay on the ejectors. The software update from Monday introduced a 15-millisecond latency in the signal processing. At 1.5 m/s, the pea travels 2.25 cm in that time. The ejector was missing the target. Fix: Reverted firmware to v4.1.1. Timing is back in sync. Yield restoring.
Tape almost out. Swapping to a fresh roll from our recovered stash.
My shift is over. Good riddance to this week. Do not touch the firmware, do not touch the speed dial. Protect the tape with your life. Have a good weekend.
